p: The arboretum was started in 1829 by Robert Holford, a wealthy Victorian landowner, and carried on by his son George. They planted for beauty and spectacle, collecting trees from across the world, and many of their original giants still tower over the paths today. Walking round, you're enjoying a garden that was planned generations ahead.

How long to allow? Two or three hours lets you see the highlights of the Old Arboretum and the treetop walkway, but you could easily spend all day if you head into Silk Wood too. The paths are generally well kept, and the walkway is a gentle incline rather than a climb, which makes it friendlier for pushchairs and wheelchairs than many viewpoints.

Autumn weekends get very busy, especially when the colour is at its peak, so try to come early in the day or midweek if you can. Dogs are welcome in some parts of the arboretum but not all, so check the rules before bringing your four-legged friend. Wellies are handy after rain, because the grass paths can get muddy.

Tetbury is the natural place to combine with a visit. It's a handsome Cotswold market town with honey-coloured stone, famous antiques shops and the pillared Market House at its heart. The King's garden at Highgrove is close by too, open for pre-booked tours at certain times of year. Fancy a bit more Cotswold charm? Malmesbury, with its abbey, is a short drive away.
